How early should you arrive at John F. Kennedy International?

For a typical domestic flight out of JFK, plan to reach the airport 84–103 minutes before departure. The hour you fly moves that number more than anything else. Below are representative arrive-by times built from how security runs at John F. Kennedy International, not a one-size-fits-all “two hours early.” For your terminal and your bag, check your exact flight.

Security and the walk to your gate at JFK

New York is a large, complex airport where security can back up and the curb-to-gate walk is long (around 30 minutes at peak). It pays to leave earlier here, especially at the busy morning and evening banks.

How these times are built

BoardFlight works backward through each step of your journey: curb to check-in, bag drop, security, and the walk to your gate. Every step is modeled for JFK and the hour you fly, then combined into a single arrive-by time. The plan is built for a busy day rather than an average one, so a normal slow morning has headroom without sending you absurdly early.

It is honest about what it knows. Parts of a flight’s plan that come from a default rather than airport data are marked as estimates. An unconfirmed delay never makes the plan riskier, because a posted delay often gets rolled back. The arrive-by time stays anchored to the scheduled departure.

Common questions about JFK

How early should I get to JFK for a domestic flight?

With no checked bag and the standard security lane, BoardFlight's representative times for JFK run from 84 to 103 minutes before departure, depending on the hour you fly. A checked bag, an international route, or PreCheck and CLEAR change that number.

Is 2 hours enough at JFK?

With a carry-on only, usually yes: BoardFlight's representative times for JFK run 84 to 103 minutes before a domestic departure. With a checked bag it can take longer, 109 to 129 minutes depending on the hour. Your airline's own check-in and bag-drop deadlines always come first.

How much earlier should I get to JFK with a checked bag?

Plan on 109 to 129 minutes before a domestic departure with one checked bag, compared with 84 to 103 minutes with a carry-on only, based on BoardFlight's representative times for JFK. The difference is the time to reach the counter and drop the bag. Your airline also sets a cutoff for checking bags before departure, so check it before you go.

How early should I get to JFK with TSA PreCheck?

With TSA PreCheck, BoardFlight's representative times for JFK run 77 to 92 minutes before a domestic departure, compared with 84 to 103 minutes in the standard lane (no checked bag). PreCheck shortens the security step; the walk to your gate and any bag drop stay the same.

How early should I get to JFK for an international flight?

Plan on more time than for a domestic flight. For an international departure from JFK, BoardFlight's representative times run 94 to 113 minutes before departure with no checked bag in the standard lane, depending on the hour. Airlines set earlier check-in and gate deadlines for international flights, and those come first, so check yours before you leave.

When is the security wait shortest at JFK?

Quietest time between 5 AM and 10 PM on Monday: around 10 PM, about 16 minutes of modeled security wait at JFK. It is the quietest point marked on the chart above. It is a planning estimate, not a live queue reading.

When is the security wait longest at JFK?

Busiest time between 5 AM and 10 PM on Monday: around 5:30 PM, about 27 minutes of modeled security wait at JFK. It is the busiest point marked on the chart above.
